newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Rate rise supports Bulgaria lev to 229-230 at closE.
newsitem.headline: Rate rise supports Bulgaria lev to 229-230 at closE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed to 229-230 per dollar at close from 230.40/80 at the opening and 234 at the previous close amid active interbank trade, supported by a record high main interest rate, dealers said.
"Relatively large volumes (of foreign currency) changed hands in active trade and the lev closed stronger between 229-230 per dollar as the new rate went in force," said a dealer. @

The central bank (BNB) on Monday hiked its central interest rate (CIR) to 300 percent annually from 108 percent, in force from Tuesday, in a bid to restore confidence in the slumping lev on the domestic market.
The BNB today bought and sold small foreign currency volumes, a BNB official told Reuters, declining to specify the exchange rates of the trade.
BNB officials told a news conference on Tuesday that the central bank would closely monitor the interbank market and intervene if the lev comes under fresh pressure. @
But they declined to say whether the BNB would just support the lev at its current levels or help it strengthen further.

"Some banks have accumulated large amounts of foreign currency bought at high exchange rates in recent months and they are still reluctant to sell, which will probably prevent a sharp lev's rise in the near term," said another dealer.
Dealers also said that the lev might resume its fall if the market does not see fresh funds coming to the country from the planned large-scale sell-offs by the year-end. @

The lev weakened to a historic low of 236.80-237 per dollar on Monday morning before the rate hike was announced from 71 at the beginning of the year. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
